body:
In article <35d90581.0@rcfnews.cs.umass.edu>,
  ehaugsja@giane.cs.umass.edu (Erik Haugsjaa) wrote:
> John Merrall (ac096@freenet.hamilton.on.ca) wrote:
> > Erik Haugsjaa (ehaugsja@giane.cs.umass.edu) wrote:
> > : Two areas where people think TK is delusional:

1. His diagnosis of modern industrial society. (People are the
problem -- they can't say no to technology.)

> > : 2. His personal plan about what to do about it. (Bomb people)
> >
> > : I have no problems with #1.  It's not delusional.  Technology is
> > : PART of being human.  But his #2 (truly delusional) means that
> > : people will (and do) take #1 as delusional as well.
> >
> > Hm? Why is it "delusional" to bomb people to make a point?
>
> Maybe delusional is a strong word, but I think TK was certainly
> incorrect in his thinking that his bombs would make the point he hoped
> for.

  "My motive for doing what I am going to do is simply personal revenge.  I
do not expect to accomplish anything by it.  Of course, if my crime (and my
reasons for committing it) gets any public attention, it may help to
stimulate public interest in the technology question and thereby improve the
chances of stopping technology before it is too late; but on the other hand,
most people will probably be repelled by  [page 277] my crime, and the
opponents of freedom may use it as a weapon to support their arguments for
control over human behavior.  I have no way of knowing whether my action will
do more good than harm.  I certainly don't claim to be an altruist or to be
acting for the "good" (whatever that is) of the human race.  I act merely
from a desire for revenge.  Of course, I would like to get revenge on the
whole scientific and [word crossed out] bureaucratic establishment, not to
mention communists and others who  [page 278] threaten freedom, but that
being impossible, I have to content myself with just a little revenge.	These
days it is fashionable to ascribe sick-sounding motivations (in many cases,
correctly, I admit) to persons who commit antisocial acts.  Perhaps some
people will deny that I am motivated by a hatred for what is happening to
freedom.  However, I think I know myself pretty well and I think they are
wrong. Let me explain more fully.  It is quite true that I do not fit into
organized society, and..." -- Exhibit 8, Ted Kaczynski's Journal, April 6
1971 (http://www.cs.umass.edu/~ehaugsja/unabom/docs/ex06-10.html)

Let me explain more fully??? What comes after the ... !!!

And when was his 1971 essay written?
His first bomb was in 1978.

Scott,

Do you believe that "psychiatric analysis of Kaczynski's writings ...
sanitize(s) them of any political content" (as you say the gov't hoped in your
article from last year)?  Why did TK feel (incorrectly?) that his
(half-hearted?) revolution was NOT political?

Re: incorrect:
"This is not to be a POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow
not governments but the economic and technological basis of the present
society." - Par. 4.

Re: half-hearted "I propose that you join me and a few other people to whom I
am writing in an attempt to found an organization dedicated to stopping
federal aid to scientific research. I realize that you will probably reject
this , but I hope that you will not reject it on the basis of some vague
dogma such as "knowledge is" READ the hope of READ. Okay, knowledge is good,
but how high a price, in terms of freedom, are	going to pay for knowledge?
You may be understandably reluctant to join an organization about which  know
nothing, but you know as much about it as I do. It hasn't been started yet.
You would be one of  founding members. I claim to have no particular
qualifications for trying to start such an organization, and I	no idea how
to go about it, I am only making an attempt because no better qualified
person has yet done  I am simply trying to bring together a few highly
intelligent and thoughtful people who would be willing to over the task. I
would prefer to drop out of it personally because I am unsuited to that kind
of work: in I dislike it intensely." - TK's 1971 essay
(http://www.cs.umass.edu/~ehaugsja/unabom/docs/1971essay.html)

So, was the trial TK got appropriate?   Should it have been a state murder
trial?  Could you discuss the implications and reasoning for the federal
anti-terrorism laws and your feelings about them?

E
